source.title: Expand Neurons, Not Parameters
source.authors: Linghao Kong; Inimai Subramanian; Yonadav G. Shavit; Micah Adler; Dan Alistarh; N. Shavit

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no evident truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether reducing neuron-level feature collisions improves representational separation in Boolean toy networks, using fixed-parameter neuron expansion and capacity, cosine, and collision measurements rather than the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: The Boolean DNF experiments directly measure feature capacity, neuron cosine similarity, collision rates, and clause-structure recovery. Accuracy-only results are recorded under fits_no_version because accuracy does not itself measure the geometry or polysemanticity named by the versions. Vision-task accuracy results, cited findings, and results about the expansion method's performance without a direct measure of feature overlap or polysemanticity are not rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: In small Boolean DNF networks with known clause features, the study varies neuron count at a fixed non-zero parameter budget. It measures feature capacity (Scherlis et al.), neuron cosine similarity, edge collisions and clause recovery. This bears on V2, whether sharing comes from limited neuron capacity. It does not test V1's sparsity transition or geometry, and the reduced sharing is partly imposed by the fixed disjoint masks the method builds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress that random splits approximate clause-split gains, so reduced collisions rather than precise assignment drive the benefit. They present FPE as a mechanistic proof of concept, not a deployment method.
record.recipe_differences: The study expands a pretrained small network by splitting neurons and partitioning incoming weights into sparse supports, then fine-tunes at fixed non-zero parameter count. It measures capacity, cosine similarity, collisions, and clause recovery; this is not a reproduction of the original toy-model setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Benefits vary with neuron count and clause count: reported gains are larger under high interference pressure, diminish as width increases, and begin to plateau beyond approximately 16 clauses in the stated sweep. Clause-aware splits outperform random splits in Boolean tasks, although their difference is less pronounced in vision experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed non-zero parameters, clause-split and random-split expansion raise Boolean accuracy over dense (99.4% and 88.7% vs 78.7%). The gains shrink with width and plateau beyond about 16 clauses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spreading a fixed parameter budget over more neurons improves accuracy when the feature-to-neuron ratio is high.

fits_no_version.finding: A non-disjoint widened baseline with the same non-zero parameters underperforms FPE and sometimes the dense model (Table A14).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The accuracy gain from widening depends on disjoint weight supports that reduce collisions, not on width alone.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The core mechanistic measurements are from small Boolean settings, with feature capacity and cosine results averaged over five trials. The authors call the circuit and semantic analyses preliminary. The study does not test the original toy-model sparsity and importance sweeps, and its feature-based splits on real data are acknowledged as heuristic.
record.rows_left_out: No additional direct V1/V2 result rows left out. Accuracy results from the other Boolean embedding experiments and vision tasks, and the dynamic-sparsity and structured-sparsity results, were not included because they do not directly measure the representational geometry or polysemanticity named by the tested versions.

untested.parts: All of it. There is no sparsity sweep, phase transition, or geometry of feature directions in a bottleneck. Cosine is measured between neuron weight vectors, not between features as nearly orthogonal directions.
Whether feature importance decides which features get dedicated dimensions. All clauses are equally important.

missing.what: Dense models' clause recovery improves as neuron count rises. This is consistent with the capacity account.
missing.locator: Section A.9, Figure A7 bottom row

missing.what: Random-split FPE lowers mean neuron cosine similarity versus dense across widths in CLIP CIFAR-100 classifiers.
Regressions of accuracy gain on capacity and cosine fold change when varying width, with R² values.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 labels are removed. Its limits_scope also cited accuracy rows (r35–r36) not linked to V1. V2 importance-based allocation is untested. The r01 dense baseline, with sub-maximal capacity at 3 clauses and 8 neurons, hints at sharing without capacity pressure (V3), but the authors do not interpret it so. The capacity definition for clause features is also ambiguous, so no V3 verdict is given. Boolean capacity and cosine results use five trials.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original toy-model sparsity-dependent phase transition, vary feature co-activation sparsity or importance, or establish a regular geometric configuration or that the measured directions are nearly orthogonal.
Tests capacity competition and reduced feature sharing in Boolean tasks, but does not test whether feature importance determines which features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not investigate alternative causes of polysemantic neurons independent of capacity pressure.
No LLM feature-distribution or SAE-recovery experiment.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not test whether the represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relationships.condition: Single-hidden-layer Boolean DNF networks, 8 neurons expanded 2x at fixed non-zero parameters, 3–32 clauses
relationships.reason: Adding neurons at fixed parameters raises feature capacity about 1.4–2.2x (r01–r16). It also cuts neuron cosine similarity (r19–r20, r23–r32) and edge collisions while improving clause recovery (r37–r39).
relationships.display_finding: Adding neurons while holding non-zero parameters fixed raised feature capacity by about 1.4x to over 2x. It also lowered neuron cosine similarity and edge collisions, and improved clause recovery.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Single-hidden-layer Boolean DNF networks, 8 neurons expanded 2x at fixed non-zero parameters, 3–32 clauses
source_check.reason: Support is appropriate, but the exact condition needs correction: Tables A1–A2 specify eight initial dense neurons without specifying the expansion factor; Section 4.2 studies both α=2 and α=4. Remove the table-specific 2x attribution. The capacity ratios extend to approximately 2.4x, rather than 2.2x.

relationships.condition: Low clause counts and the engineered, fixed disjoint-mask intervention
relationships.reason: Cosine drops are within error at 12 and 32 literals (r17, r18, r21, r22). Sharing is partly removed by the construction itself, not shown to arise from training. The dense 3-clause model uses only 1.896 of 3 capacity even with 8 neurons (r01).
relationships.display_finding: Drops in neuron cosine similarity were within error at 12 and 32 literals, and part of the sharing was removed by the engineered construction rather than by training. The dense 3-clause model used only 1.896 of a possible 3 capacity even with 8 neurons.

source_check.condition: Low clause counts and the engineered, fixed disjoint-mask intervention
source_check.reason: r01 shows increased capacity, and r17, r18, r21 and r22 all show lower mean cosine similarity. Overlapping unspecified uncertainty ranges do not establish a limiting result. The engineered intervention and untested origin of sharing are evidential limitations, not demonstrated conditions where V2 fails or needs qualification.

relation.reason: The study reports its own representational measurements bearing on V2, beyond reporting expansion accuracy.

tranche.reason: Fixed-parameter neuron expansion is a different intervention bearing on the capacity account, with direct measurements of feature capacity, neuron similarity, collisions and clause recovery.

source_check.notes: Tables A1–A2 leave the expansion factor and meaning of ± unspecified; their cells are readable. Importance-ranked allocation is untested, and the text does not explicitly establish the r01 note's claimed maximum capacity of three.

statements.correction: Table A2: mean cosine similarity decreases under both splits at 12 and 32 literals; displayed uncertainty ranges overlap. Table A1: dense capacity at 12 literals is 1.896 ± 0.377 with eight initial neurons. Section 2.2: input supports are partitioned by fixed disjoint masks. Importance-ranked allocation is untested.
statements.problem: The numerical facts and intervention caveat are accurate, but they do not establish a limits_scope result. Overlapping unspecified uncertainty ranges do not establish a failed or incomplete reduction, and unused measured capacity does not by itself identify why sharing arose.
